description: Focus-dependent historical benchmarks for game years 0-600 (about 5000-1500 BCE). A society that pours itself into one research line or a mixed archetype is judged against what comparable societies achieved with that emphasis: higher bands on its focus metrics, lower bands elsewhere, and at least one required cost below the base typical. Human summary and calibration notes: docs/research/BENCHMARKS_FOCUS_600.md. Resolver and validator: tools/research/focus_bench.py.

position_scale.meaning: a band position on the base band's own scale, oriented so larger is better ('neither' metrics: numerically larger)

anchors.-2: worse plausibility bound (min; max for 'lower' metrics)
anchors.2: better plausibility bound (max; min for 'lower' metrics)

position_scale.interpolation: linear between anchors, geometric for metrics listed as 'log' in metric_scales; positions interpolate linearly between years
position_scale.modifier: [low_pos, typical_pos, high_pos]; min and max never move; an omitted metric is neutral [-1, 0, 1]
position_scale.construction: each focus metric uses a named preset (the "presets" table: [low, typical, high] positions at full effect) scaled by the "ramp": by_year = neutral + ramp[year] x (preset - neutral). Ramp 0 at year 0 (the 120 founders are identical whatever the player will choose), 0.5 at 100, 0.85 at 300, 1.0 at 600. The 600-1200 file copies these year-600 positions as its own 600 row so the band is continuous at the join.

ramp.note: by_year positions = neutral + ramp x (full - neutral): founders are identical at year 0, a focus shows half its effect after one century and all of it by 600

roles.boost: focus metric: effective typical above the base typical; may pass the effective high by allowed_lead.boosted x |high - typical|
roles.neutral: base band (possibly with a raised floor or lowered ceiling); base allowed_deviation applies
roles.cost: effective typical below the base typical; no lead past the (lowered) high
roles.shift: 'neither' metric moved up or down (e.g. more people under arms); must stay inside the shifted low..high
roles.context: reserved for era-wide records; the 0-600 file uses none: here largest_settlement_historical is read as the largest settlement a society with this focus reached (calibrated to comparable societies) and major_innovations_per_century as innovations it originated. The 600-1200 file treats both as context and fades these 0-600 effects out by 700.

classification.rule: share = emphasis units on a line / all units (the research_emphasis order). 1) An archetype matches when its lines hold >= 55% combined, >= 12% each, and no line holds >= 40%; the best combined share wins. 2) Otherwise every line with share >= 25% gets weight min(1, (share - 1/12) / (0.40 - 1/12)); any remaining weight goes to 'balanced'; weights are normalised and the focus is that blend (positions are averaged). 3) Nothing >= 25%: balanced. A line focus's labor/decree 'signature' adds 0.15 to its line's share in step 2 only (archetypes are matched on the raw research shares). Timed strategies are classified per phase: judge a century by the phase active during most of it.
classification.explicit: a strategy dict with "focus_id" (a focus name or a {focus: weight} blend) is judged under it; strategy_spec "focus" is the settlement focus (government_people_system.gd), not a benchmark focus

knowledge.definition: The society puts its observers and record keepers first: calendars, counting, notation, systematic observation of sky, plants and materials. Operationally: >= 40% of research emphasis units on knowledge (share = units on the line / all units).

knowledge.calibration: Early calendrical and record-keeping communities: specialist observers 1-3% of adults; tokens, tallies and proto-notation; 4-6 notable innovations per century at the very best; literacy never above about 1-2% of adults before 1500 BCE-equivalent. The observers come out of building, crafts and the watch, so monuments stay small and growth slightly slower.

shock_hazard_mult_doc: Per focus, optional multipliers on the per-century shock hazards of tools/sim/shocks/catalog.py (ancient band; the same keys as benchmarks_1200.json shock_widening.hazard_per_game_century). Values match the 600-1200 file for the same focus so the join is continuous: connected trade societies suffer more epidemics, redistributive economies more systemic collapse, stewards fewer famines, isolated peoples fewer epidemics, collapses and wars. Lower is better; focus_bench.py counts them as dimensions in the pairwise dominance check. A blend uses the weighted geometric mean.
allowed_lead_doc: allowed_lead.boosted (x |effective high - effective typical|) is the lead past the effective high on boosted metrics; per_metric overrides it; neutral metrics keep benchmarks_600.json facet_over_high_fraction (0.15); cost and shifted metrics get none. milestone_early_fraction is ABSOLUTE (same representation as the 600-1200 file): registry items in the focus lines (strategy.lines) may land up to focus_lines x design year early, others up to other_lines (= base 0.2), never before band_low.
